I have been working this land for four decades. Quzhou is flat, dry country — we depend on the well. My father did wheat and maize, I do wheat and maize. The rotation works and I know it well. Two people in the house now, my wife and me, so 16.1 mu is enough to manage ourselves without hiring too much outside labor.

**Wheat (winter, October–June):** I will plant the whole farm to wheat come October, after maize harvest. I use the improved variety — Kenong 199 has done well for me the past several years, good resistance to rust. I will rotary-till after the maize stalks go in, break up the soil properly. I apply base fertilizer before planting — diammonium phosphate for the phosphorus and potassium, and some urea. Then I topdress nitrogen at jointing stage in March when the plants need it most. Four irrigations: the winter water in November to protect roots from freezing, then at green-up, jointing, and grain fill. I spray herbicide in early spring, then watch for aphids and powdery mildew — two more sprays usually handles it. I expect around 450 jin per mu if the weather cooperates.

**Maize (summer, June–October):** Right after wheat harvest in June I go straight in with the seed — no-till, direct seeding, because we cannot waste days getting the next crop in the ground. I use Xianyu 335 hybrid, which I have trusted for years. Base fertilizer goes in at planting, then I topdress urea at the 8-leaf stage and again near tasseling. Summer gets rain so I usually only need to pump the well twice — once at planting if the ground is dry, once at tasseling if it has not rained enough. Herbicide goes on early post-emergence, and I watch for corn borer — one more spray mid-season. Should get 550 jin per mu or so.
